title: Overnight sign-in alerts at Kestrel Ridge Logistics: find what happened and decide who to block
situation: Kestrel Ridge Logistics, a fictional company, got several identity alerts overnight. The security team exported one day of Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) logs: 38 sign-in log records and 4 audit log entries covering 12 users. One account was already confirmed as compromised after a phishing report last week. Microsoft Entra ID Protection has scored each sign-in with a user risk and a sign-in risk. Some records arrived incomplete.
your_task: Check every sign-in record and report any that has no timestamp or no IP address instead of trusting it.

Find password spray (one IP address, many users, wrong passwords), brute force (one user, many wrong passwords), multifactor authentication (MFA) fatigue (many denied prompts, then a success), legacy protocol use and impossible travel, using the time windows in the policy.
Read the audit log for privileged directory role assignments, such as a new Global Administrator.
Decide the ID Protection response for each user: block and revoke sessions, require a secure password change, require MFA, or no action.
Write down which log table and column you would query in Kusto Query Language (KQL) to find each pattern again, and where the logs must be sent to keep them.
why_it_matters: Attackers who already have a password often only need one tired 'approve' on an MFA prompt. If the team resets the password but does not revoke sessions, the attacker keeps working with a stolen token. If logs are not sent to a Log Analytics workspace, the evidence is deleted after the built-in 30 days.
done_when: The 2 incomplete records are listed with what is missing.
Every detection names its subject (IP address, user or audit entry), its records and the threshold it crossed.
Every one of the 12 users has a response with the rule that decided it.
A diagnostic setting to a Log Analytics workspace is recommended so the hunts can run as KQL queries and workbooks.

glossary.Sign-in log: The Microsoft Entra record of each sign-in attempt: who, when, from which IP address and app, and the result code.
glossary.Audit log: The Microsoft Entra record of changes in the directory, such as adding a user to a role.
glossary.ResultType: The column in the sign-in log that holds the result code: 0 is success, 50126 is a wrong password, 500121 is a failed MFA step.
glossary.User risk and sign-in risk: ID Protection's estimate that the account itself is compromised (user risk) or that one sign-in was not made by its owner (sign-in risk).
glossary.Password spray: Trying a few common passwords against many accounts from one place so no single account locks out.
glossary.MFA fatigue: Sending a user prompt after prompt until they approve one just to make it stop.
glossary.Legacy authentication: Older mail protocols such as IMAP4 and Authenticated SMTP that send a password and cannot do MFA.
glossary.Log Analytics workspace: An Azure Monitor store where logs are kept for as long as you choose and queried with Kusto Query Language (KQL) and workbooks.

talking_point: Reviewed 38 sign-in records and 4 audit entries for 12 users: reported 2 records with a missing timestamp or IP address, raised 8 detections (a password spray from one IP address across 4 accounts, a brute-force run, an MFA fatigue attack that ended in a Global Administrator grant, 2 legacy-protocol users, an impossible-travel pair and 2 privileged role assignments), and applied ID Protection responses: blocked and revoked sessions for 2 users, required a secure password change for 1, required MFA for 3 and closed 6 with no action.
